claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys can exhibit dual-phase lamellar microstructures.
The numerous internal boundaries in the lamellar colonies are prone to microcrack initiation during tensile loading.
An optimized post-solidification isothermal hold followed by rapid quenching will induce nanoscale precipitates at lamellar-colony internal boundaries.
Nanoscale precipitates can occur in a lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The nanoscale precipitates will preferentially form along internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Rapid quenching will freeze and retain the beneficial precipitate distribution produced during the isothermal hold.
Boundary nanoscale precipitates enhance the cohesion of the internal boundaries.
Boundary nanoscale precipitates impede stress concentration at internal boundaries.
Boundary nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation pile-up.
Improved boundary cohesion and reduced stress concentration or dislocation pile-up will reduce microcrack initiation during tensile loading.
The heat-treated alloy will have higher room-temperature tensile strength than the as-cast alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the as-cast alloy.
Simultaneously high room-temperature tensile strength and ductility are achievable in at least one lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The effectiveness of the treatment depends on alloy composition, annealing temperature, hold duration, and cooling rate.
Processing outside the optimal window may produce insufficient precipitation or undesirable precipitate coarsening.
The quantitative property improvements and optimal temperature, duration, and quench rate remain undetermined.
